name: EU AI Act risk-based classification
version: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as published; Omnibus 2026 changes not reflected
description: The AI Act classifies AI systems by the level of risk of their use (unacceptable, high, transparency, minimal) and adds a separate regime for general-purpose AI models. Unlike the other taxonomies here it classifies systems and uses, not types of harm.

categories.name: Unacceptable risk (prohibited practices, Art. 5)
categories.description: AI practices banned in the EU.

children.name: Subliminal, manipulative or deceptive techniques causing significant harm
Exploiting vulnerabilities due to age, disability or social or economic situation
Social scoring leading to detrimental or unfavourable treatment
Predicting criminal offences based solely on profiling or personality traits
Untargeted scraping of facial images to build facial recognition databases
Emotion recognition in the workplace and education (except medical or safety reasons)
Biometric categorisation inferring sensitive characteristics
Real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement (narrow exceptions)

categories.name: High risk (Art. 6, Annexes I and III)
categories.description: Allowed subject to requirements: risk management, data governance, documentation, logging, transparency, human oversight, accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity.

children.name: Safety components of products under EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I)
Biometrics (Annex III.1)
Critical infrastructure (Annex III.2)
Education and vocational training (Annex III.3)
Employment, workers' management and access to self-employment (Annex III.4)
Access to essential private and public services and benefits, incl. credit scoring and insurance (Annex III.5)
Law enforcement (Annex III.6)
Migration, asylum and border control (Annex III.7)
Administration of justice and democratic processes (Annex III.8)

categories.name: Transparency risk (Art. 50)
categories.description: Disclosure duties for certain AI systems.

children.name: AI systems interacting with people must disclose that they are AI
Synthetic audio, image, video and text must be machine-readably marked
Deployers of emotion recognition or biometric categorisation must inform people exposed
Deep fakes and AI-generated text on matters of public interest must be disclosed

categories.name: Minimal risk
categories.description: No new obligations; voluntary codes of conduct encouraged.

categories.name: General-purpose AI models (Art. 53)
categories.description: Documentation, copyright policy and training-content summary for all GPAI model providers.

children.name: Technical documentation and information for downstream providers
Copyright policy and public summary of training content

categories.name: GPAI models with systemic risk (Art. 55)
categories.description: Additional duties above the 10^25 FLOP presumption or by designation.

children.name: Model evaluation including adversarial testing
Assess and mitigate systemic risks at Union level
Track and report serious incidents
Adequate cybersecurity for the model and its infrastructure

record_provenance.notes: Hand-authored by the compiler from the publication. Item labels are short paraphrases of the Articles and Annex headings, not verbatim text.
